issues.description:
Method return type mismatch for Animal.messageOnFeed():
- Problem statement UML and task text declare Animal.messageOnFeed() as returning a String (problem_statement.md shows the abstract method signature messageOnFeed():String).
- The solution implementation declares the abstract method as public abstract FeedResponse messageOnFeed() (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java), and introduces a FeedResponse class (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/FeedResponse.java).
- Individual solution subclasses are inconsistent: Pig and Seal implement messageOnFeed() returning FeedResponse, while Goat implements messageOnFeed() returning String (solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Pig.java, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java, src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java).
This inconsistency (String vs FeedResponse) will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the expected API: whether messageOnFeed() should return a plain String message (as the exercise text/UML indicate) or a FeedResponse object (as the provided solution does).
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the return type of messageOnFeed() consistent across problem statement, template, and solution. Two viable resolutions:
Option A (preferable to match the UML/text): change the solution to use String as the return type for messageOnFeed():
- Update solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java to declare public abstract String messageOnFeed();
- Remove or stop using FeedResponse (delete FeedResponse.java) and update Seal.java and Pig.java to return the String messages (e.g., "Arf Arf!", "Oink!") instead of FeedResponse objects.
- Ensure Goat.java already returning String remains consistent and compiles.
Option B (if FeedResponse is intentional): update the problem statement and UML to specify messageOnFeed(): FeedResponse and document FeedResponse fields; then update Goat.java to return FeedResponse and update any template/tests to expect FeedResponse.
Apply one of these consistently so all Animal subclasses and callers use the same return type to avoid compilation errors and confusion.
